analysis_role: Post-outcome interpretation of prespecified physical predictions; no phenotype measurements or new optimization.
interpretations: Forward adenosine or inosine phosphorolysis individually permits RBK deletion growth in this glucose model. Both together also rescue; reverse catalysis is not required for the observed rescue.
Deleting PP_4248 or rolling back both added reactions while RBK is disabled returns zero growth, identifying the added chemistry as necessary for this conditional rescue.
AhcY deletion with RBK deletion removes rescue in every PpnP arm. ADA deletion removes rescue only in the inosine-only arm. Inosine hydrolase deletion does not remove the PpnP rescue.

PPM deletion does not remove rescue because selected witnesses use reverse PNP, RNMK and NMNN; PNP and NMNN lack GPRs. The model therefore cannot use this outcome to validate PP_1777 phosphopentomutase activity.
Closing RHCYS alone preserves WT growth via AHCi/ADA/INSH/RBK but retains RBK dependence. PpnP rescue remains with RHCYS closed. AhcY becomes essential in the RHCYS-closed WT physical contexts.

PpnP and RBK single deletions each remain viable in the main candidate arm, while their combined deletion does not. These are conditional model predictions, not experimentally established synthetic lethality.
PP_4248 is unrepresented in parent arms: their rbk_ppnp record is missing/uninterpretable, not a measured or simulated biological nonessentiality result.

Selected fluxes are single optimal witnesses, not unique pathways or measured cellular fluxes. Small differences in optimized WT growth do not establish enzyme capacity, energetic preference in vivo or predictive benefit.
limitations: Homology-based KT2440 PpnP function; unresolved original reverse-assay evidence.
PP_1777 substrate activity and gene-less salvage reactions are inherited uncertainties.
Zero positive ATP-maintenance lower bound; fixed glucose medium; unconstrained enzyme capacities.
Quinone-demand amount and upstream/source quinone chemistry remain provisional.
This interpretation uses no benchmark outcomes and makes no independent-validation or field-advancement claim.
method: Read saved JSON and SBML with the Python standard library. Sum exact rational coefficients parsed directly from serialized SBML. Compare saved selected-flux witnesses by arithmetic only. No solver, model runner, biochemical curation or fitness table used.

proposed_discriminating_experiments.distinguishes: PpnP substrate activity independently of all downstream PPM and salvage assumptions.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.proposal: Purify the sequence-verified PP_4248 protein; test adenosine and inosine separately with and without phosphate; directly identify bases and ribose-1-P. Include no-enzyme and free-ribose-plus-phosphate controls. Test reverse synthesis separately to resolve directionality.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.question: Does KT2440 PP_4248 catalyze the proposed reactions?

proposed_discriminating_experiments.distinguishes: PP_1777 phosphopentomutase activity versus a mere family annotation; a positive PpnP assay does not answer this.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.proposal: Assay purified sequence-verified PP_1777 with ribose-1-P and its annotated mannose-phosphate substrates, identifying the correct product isomer and measuring substrate-dependent rates.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.question: Can PP_1777 carry ribose-1-P to ribose-5-P at relevant capacity?

proposed_discriminating_experiments.distinguishes: Direct mutase flux versus the modelled ATP-consuming nicotinamide cycle. A PP_1777 deletion alone is not decisive because the model has this alternative.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.proposal: In a follow-up design, trace labeled ribose-1-P into ribose-5-P and candidate nicotinamide intermediates in cell extracts while independently restricting PPM and RNMK activity; establish identities and activity of the currently gene-less PNP/NMNN edges before assigning genetic interventions. This avoids assuming cellular uptake of supplied ribose-1-P.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.question: Can a cell extract use the alternative ATP-dependent r1p disposal route?

proposed_discriminating_experiments.distinguishes: A physiological contribution of the proposed PpnP bypass versus biochemical activity that is insufficient, unexpressed, or replaced by other routes in vivo.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.proposal: After enzyme identities are established, compare matched KT2440 wild type, rbk, ppnP and rbk/ppnP perturbations with complementation, growth and targeted intracellular SAH/nucleoside/ribose-phosphate measurements in the declared condition. Keep the PPM/salvage question separate.
proposed_discriminating_experiments.question: Does PpnP contribute to methyl-cycle disposal in cells?

ribosyl_bound_proof.additional_implications: The nested rows prove why RBK+AhcY blocks every PpnP arm and why RBK+ADA blocks the inosine-only arm, where PUNP1 is absent. These are model-balance implications, not measured cellular requirements.
ribosyl_bound_proof.basis: Each quinone tail methylation has equal flux t=epsilon*Growth; the three methylations each supply one unit to the five-species row sum; all 11 other positive row terms have nonnegative flux. Only RBK/PUNP1/PUNP5 have negative coefficients.
ribosyl_bound_proof.inequality: v_RBK + v_PUNP1 + v_PUNP5 >= 3 * epsilon * v_Growth; absent PUNP reactions have zero flux. PUNP values are signed in the reversible arm.
ribosyl_bound_proof.rollback_implication: At RBK=0 and all added PUNP fluxes=0, exact positive steady-state growth is impossible. RHCYS has zero weighted coefficient, so closing it does not by itself remove this necessary constraint.
ribosyl_bound_proof.scope: Necessary model balance constraint; not biological essentiality. Additional probe demand adds a quinone drain and changes the no-drain equality.
